exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean birth)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 67 mothers who had term, singleton livebirths without hypertensive disorders or peripartum infections between 2012 and 2018.
finding: Maternal leukocyte telomere lengths (LTLs) were significantly shorter in postpartum week 1 and up to 6 months postpartum following cesarean delivery compared to vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with maternal LTLs that were nearly 500 bp shorter in postpartum week 1, and this difference persisted for several weeks postpartum.
